name: Fever grass (lemongrass) tea for fever
what_people_do: Drink fever grass (Cymbopogon citratus) tea to bring down a fever, often for children, with a shared home tradition of "sweating it out".
why_they_say_it_works: It is a cooling, aromatic herb believed to break a fever.

documented_by.source: Clement YN et al 2015, J Ethnobiol Ethnomed, PMID 26369926 (TRAMIL survey, Trinidad)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Cymbopogon citratus (with Neurolaena lobata) met the TRAMIL 20% threshold for fever among 450 Trinidad households.

documented_by.source: Mahabir D, Gulliford MC 1997, Rev Panam Salud Publica, PMID 9128111
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Fever grass was one of the plants preferentially used for non-diabetes indications by Trinidad diabetes patients.

evidence.finding: My search found nothing: one PubMed query ("lemongrass Cymbopogon citratus fever randomized") returned zero hits. Positive control: the TRAMIL query returned results in the same session.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Fever in a baby or a fever that lasts needs a doctor; a tea is no substitute (general advice).
gaps: One search only; a fuller lemongrass search is a to-do.
